title:
Two Directors, One Oscar: Can Lord and Miller, Los Javis, Fielder and
 Oppenheim or the Esiri Brothers Break Through?
summary: Co-directing teams gain Oscar momentum, reflecting growing acceptance of shared directing credits and opportunities for partnerships.
content: Awards Circuit Column: The Academy’s Directors Branch has given best director to a duo only three times in 98 years. This season, four teams are vying for attention Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Phil Lord and Chris Miller and Nigeria’s Esiri brothers are chasing a prize the Academy’s Director Branch has handed to a duo only three times in its history. Looking at the two-name directing teams in this year’s Oscar race, artistic collaboration seems to be having a moment. Not everyone sees it that way. Related Stories ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem’ Duo Praise Neon’s Strategy to Reach Young Audiences How Soviet TV Audiences Fell Under the Spell of Mass Hypnosis Artist Anatoly Kashpirovskiy “If you need two of you to make the film, then I think that’s a problem,” one prominent member of the Directors Branch bluntly tells Variety. Fielder and Oppenheim turned Elizabeth Holmes’ saga into the slippery A24 documentary “ You Can See Everything .” Calvo and Ambrossi, the Spanish duo known as Los Javis, are carrying their country’s international feature hopes with “ La Bola Negra .” Lord and Miller reunited behind the camera for Amazon MGM’s sci-fi swing “Project Hail Mary.” And twin brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri helmed Neon’s ambitious “Clarissa,” a reimagining of “Mrs. Dalloway.” All four teams face a stubborn piece of Academy history: The Directors Branch does not like splitting statuettes. In 98 years, only four directing duos have received best director nominations (one of them twice). This year, several are within earshot of nods. Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins got there first for 1961’s “West Side Story.” Their partnership was so combustible that Robbins was fired mid-production for running over schedule and budget. He retained his credit and collected the Oscar. Warren Beatty and Buck Henry followed with “Heaven Can Wait” (1978), but lost to Michael Cimino (“The Deer Hunter”). title: Teyana Taylor Sells Female-Driven Comedy to Warner Bros. (Exclusive)
summary: Teyana Taylor sets a female-led comedy at Warner Bros., co-writing, producing, and likely directing—opening casting and staffing prospects.
content: Teyana Taylor is plotting her next moves as a filmmaker. The Oscar-nominated actress has sold an original comedy pitch to Warner Bros . that she will co-write and produce via her The Aunties banner alongside producing partner Coco Gilbert. Taylor would also likely direct the project, described as a female-driven, wish fulfillment comedy that explores the chaos of modern dating, and which draws upon stories Taylor has logged from friends, family, homegirl group chats, and her own experiences. The project is in early development at Warners and specific plot details are being kept under wraps. Related Stories Movies 'You've Got Mail' Reboot in the Works at Warner Bros. Business Pam Abdy Laments Exits of Top Female Executives in Hollywood: "It Is Upsetting to See" Taylor earned an Oscar nomination earlier this year for One Battle After Another , which won multiple Oscars, including best picture as well as best director and best adapted screenplay for filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson. The role of revolutionary Perfidia Beverly Hills also earned Taylor a Golden Globe and a BET Award. The Grammy nominee came up in the world of music, and had already amassed a number of acting credits, but the film and its accolades put her acting career on a whole new trajectory. Since then, she’s been focused on her directorial debut, the Paramount feature Get Lite . The film is in post-production as it heads toward an Aug. 20 2027 release date. It stars Storm Reid and per the logline, centers on “a talented, but sheltered, dance student” who “finds inspiration, love, and family in the last place he expected: the subways of New York City.” It also stars NFL prospect Ceyair Wright.

title: 'Gilded Age' Scores Early Season 5 Renewal at HBO
summary: HBO renews The Gilded Age for Season 5, ensuring continued roles and hiring for period-drama actors and crew.
content: The news comes after the period drama has aired just three of its eight episodes for Season 4. This marks the earliest renewal announcement for the show to date, which has continued to grow its audience season to season. Per HBO, Season 4 is averaging 5.9 million U.S. multiplatform viewers per episode to date, with episode three hitting 4.3 million viewers in three days time. The episodic average is up nearly 20% over Season 3, though there are still five more episodes to air. title: Brooks Nader Joins ‘Playmates’ Movie at Searchlight (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Searchlight’s Playmates adds Brooks Nader to its cast, signaling active production and further casting opportunities.
content: Brooks Nader is the latest addition to the cast of the upcoming Searchlight movie “ Playmates ,” Variety has learned exclusively. The film is inspired by writer and director Lorraine Nicholson’s childhood experiences at the Playboy Mansion. Nader will appear alongside previously announced cast members Lily-Rose Depp, Bill Pullman, Jessica Biel, Indiana Elle, and Anna Van Patten. The official logline for “Playmates” states, “Elle (Elle), a thirteen-year-old know-it-all who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home, meets Anna (Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month. The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.” Related Stories India’s ‘How Love Moves’ Among Top Winners at IDFA Industry Section Awards IDFA Head on How ‘You Can See Everything’ Phenomenon Can Pump New Blood Into Theatrical Doc Releases: ‘What Else Would This Audience See?’ Pullman will star as Playboy founder Hugh Hefner, with Biel playing Hefner’s wife. Exact details on Nader’s character are being kept under wraps. Nader will next be seen in Fox’s reboot of “Baywatch,” which will debut on the broadcast network on Jan. 6. She originally found success as a model, including appearing in the iconic Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue. She also currently stars in the Freeform reality series “Love Thy Nader,” which is prepping a second season, and also appeared in the 33rd season of “Dancing with the Stars.” She is repped by WME, Dixon Talent, Inc. and by Leigh Fidler, Chief Brand Officer of Nader Sisters Inc. Searchlight Pictures is the studio behind “Playmates.” As mentioned above, Nicholson will write and direct. Alex Orlovsky and Duncan Montgomery will produce via High Frequency Entertainment, with Depp producing in addition to starring. title: ‘GTA 6’ Hits Massive $3.79 Billion in First-Day Sales
summary: GTA 6’s record-shattering launch underscores booming game budgets and rising demand for voice and performance-capture talent.
content: Crime pays: Rockstar Games’ “ Grand Theft Auto 6″ preorder and first-day sales reached $3.79 billion, the game developer announced Friday. Per Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two Interactive, that total sets “a new record for entertainment across any medium” and makes “ GTA 6 ” “the biggest entertainment launch in history.” A spokesperson for Take-Two Interactive declined to comment on the number of “GTA 6” copies sold. Related Stories Berlin Winner Tatiana Huezo Close to Completing Road Movie ‘Galerna’ Following Awards Boost: ‘I’m Dying to Finish It’ ‘White Tiger Column’ Directors on How Myanmar’s Resistance Speaks to Political Youth Movements in Brazil, Serbia and the U.S.: ‘Revolution Is on the Lips of a Lot of People’ For the sake of comparison, Sony Pictures’ “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” reaped $2.52 billion at the global box office in 2026, the No. 1 movie of the year to date. Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster “The Odyssey” has taken in just over $1.8 billion to date. On its first day of release, “GTA 6” made roughly as much as James Cameron’s last two “Avatar” movies, “The Way of Water” and “Fire and Ash,” have grossed combined. With just Day 1 sales, “GTA 6” has already out-grossed the highest grossing movie of all time, “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion), in one day. The game cost a reported $1.5 billion to produce over more than a decade of development. “GTA 6” launched Thursday for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and was also available on Xbox One via Xbox’s Cloud Gaming service. The game retails at $80 for the standard edition and $100 for the ultimate version. Preorders for “GTA 6” opened June 25. title: ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch
summary: Disclosure Day favored practical stunts with seamless VFX, underscoring collaboration and planning actors need for action-heavy shoots.
content: Even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a new popcorn blockbuster like “ Disclosure Day ,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences. One of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’ How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation “With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler said. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.” But while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic. “When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he said. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.” More coverage from IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables will be published here over the coming weeks. title: Robert Pattinson’s Bond Ascent: How Pricey Screen Tests and Amazon Execs Landed a Starry 007
summary: High-cost screen tests and Amazon leadership shaped Bond casting, signaling streamer-led franchise decisions and rigorous audition stakes.
content: What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life? For Robert Pattinson , there were about 12 hours between the Sunday phone call confirming he’d landed the role of James Bond and Amazon MGM’s Monday-morning release of the first image of the actor rocking a tuxedo and pistol. He spent it, rather predictably, watching an arthouse horror film. Related Stories Laura Poitras Turns Lens on ICE's 'Paramilitary Occupation' of Minneapolis in 'They’re Here' Berlin Winner Tatiana Huezo Close to Completing Road Movie ‘Galerna’ Following Awards Boost: ‘I’m Dying to Finish It’ His longtime friend and collaborator Robert Eggers told Variety this week that Pattinson was screening the director’s forthcoming genre drama “Werwulf” when the Bond news broke. Nothing like a stark naked Aaron Taylor-Johnson terrorizing a quaint village to pass the time. But after months (years, really) of toiling and speculation over who would replace Daniel Craig in the film adaptations of Ian Fleming’s spy novels, Pattinson took the crown. It buttons up a delicious, messy and very public guessing game over which lucky man would land the iconic role. When Amazon MGM bought out rights to James Bond from longtime custodians the Broccoli family in 2025, intentions were set for a young star who could shoulder the franchise for a decade or two. An A-list team of producers (Amy Pascal of “Spider-Man” and David Heyman of the “Harry Potter” movies) recruited Denis Villeneuve to direct. Together, with significant influence from Amazon execs Courtenay Valenti and Mike Hopkins (and yes, Jeff Bezos), they screen-tested a laundry list of virile performers — including Callum Turner, Tom Francis, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor — earlier this year. For the curious, the batch of screen tests cost Amazon MGM between $300,000 and $500,000 to pull off, ostensibly in secret (everyone found out), sources familiar with the process say. title: E. Lockhart, Gotham Group Tackling Fantasy Novel ‘The Curse Workers’ for 20th Television (Exclusive)
summary: 20th Television developing Holly Black’s Curse Workers trilogy with E. Lockhart and Gotham Group, creating fantasy series casting opportunities.
content: 20 th Television is in development on The Curse Workers , the best-selling fantasy books from Holly Black , with a plan to adapt it for a TV series to stream on Disney+. E. Lockhart, the author turned showrunner behind Prime Video’s hit We Were Liars , will adapt the trilogy into a series, serving as writer and executive producer. Also exec producing are Ellen Goldsmith-Vein and Jeremy Bell for The Gotham Group. The project marks a reunion for Gotham Group and Black; the company produced the 2023 series adaptation of The Spiderwick Chronicles , based on the children’s series that Black co-wrote with Tony DiTerlizzi. Related Stories TV War Is Coming in the 'Percy Jackson' Season 3 Trailer TV Series Based on Rick Riordan's 'Kane Chronicles' in the Works at Disney+ Curse Workers is set in a world where magic is illegal and controlled by the Mob. The story centers on Cassel Sharpe, the youngest son of a criminal family and the only one without magic. When his mother returns from prison, his brothers start acting strange, and his own memories are no longer making sense, forcing him to rely on his knowledge of con artistry to uncover the truth. Lockhart is the New York Times bestselling author who wrote the book sensation We Were Liars , and then was intimately involved in the book’s translation to mystery thriller series, which reached No. 1 on Prime Video and was quickly renewed for a second season, now in production. Lockhart wrote the season one finale, participated in casting and location scouting, and continues as an executive producer on season two, which incorporates the story of her prequel novel, Family of Liars . In addition to Liars , Lockhart is adapting her own novel Again Again for Wayfarer Entertainment while novel Genuine Fraud is in development as a series at Prime Video, with Rain Spencer attached to star and Sinead Daly writing the pilot. One of the biggest names in fantasy, Black is known for her New York Times best-sellers including Novels of Elfhame
